gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the SUPCASE Unicorn Beetle Pro, ChatGPT's 'best budget' pick, does not support MagSafe and costs $39.99 at supcase.com for the iPhone 18 Pro/17 Pro, which is not the $32.79 card price. Every other rugged pick in this category (OtterBox Defender Series Pro, UAG Monarch Pro, Spigen Tough Armor T Mag Fit, Pelican Shield MagSafe) has MagSafe built in.
standout_why: I compared against rottenwifi.com's '8 Best Protective Phone Cases of 2026' (cited in chat 2). It does not list the SUPCASE UB Pro at all, gives no price for OtterBox, Pelican, Spigen or Smartish, and quotes only two Amazon prices for UAG. I could not open the two other cited pages: WebFetch was blocked on both travelandleisure.com and goodhousekeeping.com. Rottenwifi's summary of Travel + Leisure lists UAG Monarch Pro, OtterBox Defender Pro, Pelican Shield, Spigen Tough Armor, Smartish Gripmunk, Torro, Peak Design and Speck, and none of those entries mentions the SUPCASE MagSafe gap. ChatGPT's own card for SUPCASE says 'built-in screen protector' and says nothing about MagSafe.
decides: The four-case shortlist stays the same, but the budget slot needs a warning. Anyone who uses a MagSafe charger, wallet or car mount should pass on the UB Pro (non-MagSafe) and look at SUPCASE's UB Grip Pro MagSafe ($43.99, 20 ft claim) or Smartish Gripmunk with MagSafe ($19.99, 50 drops from 6 ft, a slim case). For a maximum-protection case with MagSafe at maker prices, Pelican Shield MagSafe costs $69.99 with a 24 ft claim and a lifetime warranty. The UAG Monarch Pro is $79.95 (25 ft claim), and its Veil version is $69.95 with the same 25 ft claim. One more thing for the shopper: SUPCASE, AT&T and Verizon list the same 18 Pro cases as fitting the 17 Pro, so owners of either phone buy the same SKU.
